scope: Native erlang:hd/1 and erlang:tl/1 outcomes, including improper cons tails. No general list traversal capability is inferred.
adaptations: Use a closed head/tail field selector after one charged nonempty-cons check. Return the existing owned child without copying, allocating or collecting. Nil and non-list operands produce native badarg; an improper tail remains a valid result.

Positively admit both exact native BIFs. Existing complete X-source list guard/extraction cases handle compiler fusion; existing generic nonallocating BIF groups handle body and Y-source guard calls. Work failure cannot become a false guard or guest badarg.

Compiler fixtures and independent OTP answers cover proper/improper lists, tuple heads/tails, empty/non-list badarg, and successful/failed X/Y guards. Check source identity/immutability and returned boxed-child survival after collection.

Successful projection and guard paths run with no allocatable heap credit and with quota or allocator denial, retaining the mandatory VM return reserve. Y guard tests enter the actual generic BIF before injection, distinguishing caller frame allocation from primitive behavior. An initial zero-reserve test setup violated the return invariant and was corrected, not used to weaken the runtime check.

Every work prefix is tested for both primitives, guest-error paths and X/Y guard success/failure. Shared-worker tests recover exact binary bytes through both head and improper tail, test exact/one-below budgets, reuse, peer survival and reclamation.
